meanings.note: belonging to the creator or signature style

examples.trans: This is the chef's signature cuisine.

examples.text: Моя авторская кухня поразит абсолютно всех.
examples.trans: My signature cuisine will amaze absolutely everyone.
This is an original creator's recipe.

meanings.note: a particular prepared food item or meal course

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.

examples.text: Он смотрит, как будто знает всё.
examples.trans: He looks as if he knows everything.

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'diet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thanks, I am on a diet today.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He talks for a long time.

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: ironic: такая интересная = look at her, how convenient
ironic: такая интересная = look at her, how convenient

examples.trans: This is a very interesting book.

examples.text: Такая интересная. Я тебе не бандит.
examples.trans: Funny you should say that. I'm no gangster for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: They have a very beautiful house.

meanings.note: for movement; где is for location

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
remarkable or different from the ordinary

examples.text: Я не вижу здесь ничего необычного.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: The chef invented an original soup recipe.
Really? I am studying the original design.
This is an original creator's recipe.

examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'упчик'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'little soup' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What an interesting pretty little soup.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)

examples.trans: Throw it out, that is pure chemicals!

examples.text: Выкинь, Даня, это же химия! В лесу — только дровами! Ну, вперёд!
examples.trans: Throw it out, Danya, that is pure chemicals! In the forest, only with firewood! Come on, forward!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'colour' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
